premise: These are the things that could not be confirmed, or that conflict, at the capture date. None of them blocks publication; all of them are published openly instead of being smoothed over.

severity_scale.high: Affects a claim a buyer would rely on, or a compliance question that needs the Associates account to settle.
severity_scale.medium: A gap or conflict that changes how a page should be read.
severity_scale.low: Housekeeping, or a figure that will drift without anyone doing anything wrong.

items.detail: The listing's Capacity field reads "6 liters" while the title and bullets read "6-quart" with two 3-quart baskets. 6 US quarts is about 5.68 litres, so the field is not a conversion of the title.
items.why_it_matters: A buyer sizing a machine against a litre-based recipe or a litre-labelled competitor is working from a number that does not match the page's own headline.
items.action: Both readings are published verbatim and the conflict is named on the product page. Not resolved by inference.
items.status: open — needs a measurement or a retailer clarification

items.detail: The title says "24 One-Touch Preset Options"; a bullet says "25 COOKING PRE-SETS".
items.why_it_matters: Preset count is a comparison point between oven-style machines. Publishing either number as fact would be publishing a coin flip.
items.action: Neither number is used as a selling point. The conflict is shown on the product page.
items.status: open

items.detail: The listing displays "There is a newer model of this item" linking to ASIN B0GL7Z4KP4.
items.why_it_matters: The supplied short link resolves to the older ASIN. A reader following the site may reach a superseded listing without being told.
items.action: Disclosed on the product page. The site does not silently switch to the newer ASIN, because the supplied link is the owner's stated intent.
items.status: needs review — owner decision on whether to point at B0GL7Z4KP4

items.detail: Neither thermometer listing has a Product Dimensions field. Probe length is also not stated.
items.why_it_matters: Probe length decides whether a thermometer reaches the centre of a large roast, and whether it can be left in a closed oven. Footprint decides whether it fits a drawer.
items.action: Left blank and marked unverified on both product pages. No value guessed.
items.status: open — check the manufacturer's own specification sheet

items.detail: No star rating was present on either page at capture time. A rating for a different ASIN appeared in a recommendation widget on the same page.
items.why_it_matters: Quoting a neighbouring product's rating is the single easiest way to publish a false number on an affiliate site.
items.action: Ratings left blank. Only ratings rendered in the page's own rating block are stored.
items.status: open — re-capture; the rating may be region- or session-dependent

items.detail: The "Specification Met" field on P5 lists roughly twenty schemes including FDA, ISO 13485 and HACCP. P4 lists NIST and NSF.
items.why_it_matters: This field is populated by the seller. It is not a certificate, and some entries (ISO 13485 covers medical devices) are unlikely to apply to a kitchen thermometer.
items.action: Shown as a seller-declared attribute, never as verified certification. See F-07 for the accuracy figure.
items.status: open — request certificates from the manufacturer

items.detail: A bullet states a NIST certification for the claimed plus-or-minus 0.5 F accuracy.
items.why_it_matters: Accuracy is the reason to buy a thermometer. A certification claim that has not been sighted is a manufacturer assertion, not a verified fact.
items.action: Published as a vendor claim, labelled as such, with the listing cited. Not repeated in editorial voice.
items.status: open — verify with NIST's own certification database or the manufacturer

items.detail: The five products span two families — three air fryers and two thermometers — across four brands.
items.why_it_matters: A site that is about both air fryers and thermometers has to justify the pairing or it reads as a list of things someone happened to have links for. The honest pairing is cooking to a target temperature, which the guides build on.
items.action: Built the site around that pairing rather than hiding the span. Whether to narrow to air fryers only is a decision for the owner.
items.status: needs review

items.detail: The resolved short-link URLs served to this session carried query parameters but no visible tag= value.
items.why_it_matters: Program Policies 2(a) requires Special Links to use the assigned Associates ID. If tag=shopnow047c-20 is not on the link, clicks earn nothing — a commercial failure, not a compliance one, but the more expensive of the two.
items.action: Nothing is called invalid. The observation is recorded and the verification is routed to the owner's dashboard.
items.status: blocked — requires the Associates account

items.detail: No first-party traffic, click, order, revenue or commission data exists for this site.
items.why_it_matters: Any conversion rate or revenue estimate would be invented. There is no baseline to optimise against yet.
items.action: No performance figure appears anywhere on the site. The campaign ledger starts empty and defined (data/campaigns.json).
items.status: open — measure after launch

items.detail: Popularity, trending and "best" claims are easy to write and hard to support; the listings themselves display dynamic badges.
items.why_it_matters: Google's people-first guidance treats exaggerated headings as a quality problem, and Program Policies 2(b) prohibits overbroad product claims.
items.action: No editorial superlatives. Where the listing shows a badge (Amazon's Choice, "1K+ bought in past month") it is quoted with the capture date and attributed to Amazon.
items.status: controlled by rule

items.detail: P1 and P2 do not state a maximum temperature; P1 states no preset count; P4 states no probe length or physical size.
items.why_it_matters: Maximum temperature decides whether a machine can finish food that needs high heat; probe length decides whether a thermometer reaches a roast's centre.
items.action: Blank and flagged. No number inferred from a similar model.
items.status: open

items.detail: The supplied links use the link.amazon domain rather than amzn.to, and their compliance status cannot be settled from outside the account.
items.why_it_matters: Program Policies 2(b) prohibits a shortening service used so that it is unclear the link goes to an Amazon Site. Whether these particular links meet that test in the enrolled workflow is unresolved.
items.action: The site publishes direct amazon.com/dp/ destinations so clarity is not in question. The short links remain the recorded provenance. Test one link in the enrolled Associates workflow and confirm destination and reporting before relying on the short form. This is a test to run, not a verdict on the links.
items.status: unresolved — needs the enrolled Associates workflow

items.detail: Both ASINs are multi-variant listings (P3: 6/8/9 qt; P5: 1/2/3/4 probes). The resolved pages are the 8 qt and 3-probe variants.
items.why_it_matters: Capacity and probe count differ by variant, and the reader will land on whichever variant Amazon defaults to at the time.
items.action: Variant span stated in the table and on each product page, with the captured variant named.
items.status: open — will drift as Amazon changes defaults

items.detail: The CHEF iQ Sense displays readings in an app; its listing's display type is "App".
items.why_it_matters: A reader without a smartphone or Wi-Fi in the kitchen is buying something they cannot fully use. That is a fit question, not a defect.
items.action: Stated plainly in the watch-outs and in the which-one-is-for-you chooser.
items.status: disclosed

items.detail: The site is served from a GitHub Pages project path (wingbangboozle1-lang.github.io/Prod3/) rather than an apex domain.
items.why_it_matters: Search engines can index it, but a project path shares a hostname with every other project on the account, and the URL is harder to say out loud than a domain.
items.action: Canonicals, sitemap and feed all use the absolute project-path URLs so nothing resolves relatively. A custom domain is a decision for the owner.
items.status: open

items.detail: No Search Console property and no analytics endpoint are configured for this site.
items.why_it_matters: Without Search Console the site cannot see which queries it is being shown for, so the next topic has to be guessed rather than read off data.
items.action: The site is built to accept both. A verification file slot and an analytics stub are documented in content/measurement.md.
items.status: blocked — requires the owner's account access

items.detail: Star ratings, rating counts, "Amazon's Choice" and "N bought in past month" figures were captured on one day and change continuously.
items.why_it_matters: A date-stamped figure is defensible; an undated one is a slow-motion error.
items.action: Every such figure carries the capture date and the listing as its source. Nothing is presented as current.
items.status: accepted — refresh on each release

items.detail: No product photography is used. The site ships typographic hero art and illustrated product placeholders instead.
items.why_it_matters: The Operating Agreement treats images and text as Program Content, and a generated or copied photograph of a product is the wrong way to close that gap. A placeholder is honest; a fake photograph is not.
items.action: Placeholders only, labelled. Real photography requires a decision on sourcing and rights.
items.status: needs review

items.detail: None of the three air fryer listings states a manufacturer warranty period.
items.why_it_matters: Warranty length is one of the few after-sale terms a buyer can compare before purchase, and its absence is a real gap in the decision rather than something to assume a default for.
items.action: Left blank in the register and on every product page. Only the CHEF iQ listing states a term (two years); it is the only warranty published anywhere on this site.
items.status: open — check the manufacturer's own product page
